note: The locale allowlist (issue 050). A locale exists here or it does not exist at all — selection may only name a key from this file, never a URL or a query parameter (the issue-041 rule). `files` is the set of domain files that locale actually ships: THE FILES THAT EXIST ARE THE SUPPORT YOU HAVE, and any key a locale does not carry falls back one hop to en-gb. `status` gates per locale, not globally: a locale flips to `live` only after a human has reviewed its qa-to-docs screenshots, so a half-finished language is visible and honestly marked rather than hidden behind a single global SOON. Labels are in the native script and there are NO FLAGS — a flag is a country, and a language is not a country (pt-PT and pt-BR would both want a different one, and English would have to pick a fight). Each locale carries a `flag`: normally a flag is a poor stand-in for a language, but the unit here is a CULTURE (language + country), so every entry genuinely names one country and the objection does not apply.
